title: The Norwich guide to a sharper skin fade
description: What to ask your barber for, how often to refresh a skin fade, and how to keep it looking clean between appointments in Norwich.

content.heading: What makes a skin fade different?
paragraphs: A skin fade blends the hair down to bare skin around the sides and back. The result is crisp, modern and especially strong when the blend follows the shape of your head instead of relying on one standard template.

The fade can start low, in the middle or high. A low fade keeps more weight and feels subtle. A mid fade creates a balanced, noticeable contrast. A high fade removes more weight and gives the strongest, sharpest outline.

content.heading: What to tell your barber
paragraphs: Bring a reference if you have one, but also explain how you style your hair day to day. Tell your barber how high you want the fade, whether you prefer a natural or sharp hairline, and how much length you want to keep on top.
Your hair texture, growth pattern and usual styling routine all affect the best finish. A short conversation before the clippers start makes the end result much more personal.

content.heading: How often should you refresh it?
paragraphs: For the cleanest possible finish, most skin fades look their sharpest for around two weeks. Booking every two to three weeks maintains the blend; waiting three to four weeks gives more growth and may require a fuller reshaping.
Between visits, avoid trying to repair the blend yourself. Keep the neckline tidy, use a light styling product on top and book the next appointment before your preferred time fills up.

content.heading: Book a skin fade in Norwich
paragraphs: 3D Cutz is at 19 Prince of Wales Road in Norwich city centre, close to Norwich railway station. Choose Skin Fade in our online booking flow to find a time that works for you.
